chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Ismail ibn Dubeys, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Allah creates the servant in the origin of creation as a disbeliever, he will not die until Allah causes him to love evil, so he approaches it. Thus, He tests him with arrogance and tyranny, so his heart becomes callous, his character becomes bad, his face becomes harsh, his vulgarity appears, his modesty decreases, and Allah uncovers his veil, and he indulges in the prohibitions and does not withdraw from them. Then he indulges in the sins of Allah and hates His obedience, and he leaps upon the people, not satiating from disputes. So ask Allah for well-being and seek it from Him.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of arrogance and divine testing in a person's character according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith as a diagnostic tool for spiritual health, linking internal states of 'hardheatedness' (ruthlessness) to external social behaviors. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the interplay between divine decree and human character, warning that persistent arrogance and harshness are precursors to a hardened heart, thereby urging believers to actively seek 'Afah' (well-being/protection) as a preventative measure against these spiritual diseases.
